reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Absolute defense for reasonable apprehension of imminent harm
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62). Establishes an absolute defense to civil liability or criminal prosecution for killing or injuring a dog upon a preponderance-of-the-evidence showing of reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful contact to oneself or acting to prevent it against another person.

headings.title: Prior trespass complaints, prima facie evidence, and notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers two prior complaints of an unleashed dog trespassing on owned, rented, leased, or residential property (with at least one motivated by safety or substantial livestock/property damage apprehension) creating prima facie evidence on subsequent trespass, plus the sheriff or animal control authority duty to notify the dog owner and the rule that failure to notify does not invalidate or limit this subsection.

headings.title: Attorney fees, costs, and expenses upon absolute defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the court to award attorney fees, court costs, and all reasonable defense expenses incurred in a criminal prosecution or civil action only if the court finds the defendant has an absolute defense under subsection 1. Independent review revised title to make explicit that the mandatory fee/cost/expense award is conditioned on the court finding an absolute defense under subsection 1.

headings.title: Exclusions for criminal activity and other injury or damage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Excludes from the absolute defense any person engaged in or attempting criminal activity at the time of apprehension, and excludes liability for damage or injury to any person or property other than the dog itself resulting from attempts to injure or kill the dog. Independent review revised title from "collateral damage" to "other injury or damage" to reflect statutory coverage of both personal injury and property damage other than the dog itself.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked preponderance-of-evidence standard, two-complaint prima facie evidence and non-invalidating owner-notice rules, conditional fee award, and criminal-activity/other-harm exclusions. Revised subsection 3 to make the subsection 1 absolute-defense condition explicit and subsection 4 to cover both personal injury and property damage beyond the dog itself; retained subsections 1 and 2.

headings.title: Strict liability, fault reduction, and 273.020 exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62). Covers strict liability of dog owners or possessors for unprovoked bites on public or lawful private property (regardless of prior viciousness or knowledge) and for proximately caused property or livestock damage, percentage reduction for the damaged party's fault, and the exclusion for dogs killing or maiming sheep or other domestic animals under section 273.020.

headings.title: Fine upon liability and cumulative remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Imposes a fine not exceeding $1,000 on any person held liable under subsection 1 and specifies that the section's remedies are in addition to and cumulative with other statutory or common-law remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked strict liability for unprovoked bites and property/livestock damage, comparative fault reduction, the section 273.020 exclusion, conditional $1,000 maximum fine, and cumulative-remedies clause. Retained both titles as accurate and properly qualified.

headings.title: Issuing dog licenses, metallic plates, and certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14548; prior revision 1929 § 12874). Covers county clerk issuance of dog licenses, numbered metallic plates, and secretary-of-state book certificates, plus required owner, dog description, year, license number, and tax details on both the certificate and book margin.

headings.title: Clerk fee retention and remittance to county treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows the county clerk to retain ten cents per license for all services under sections 273.040 to 273.180 and requires paying the balance and other sums received, less listed supply and transmission costs, to the county treasurer.

headings.title: County dog license fund and preservation of damage suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the county treasurer to hold receipts in a separate County Dog License Fund restricted to compensating county livestock or poultry losses caused by dogs up to market value, authorizes county commission warrants only as provided, and preserves suits at law for dog-caused livestock or poultry damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14548; 1929 § 12874) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked clerk issuance and margin-record duties, 10-cent retention and expense deductions under sections 273.040 to 273.180, County Dog License Fund market-value cap, and the closing proviso preserving suits at law. Retained all three titles as accurate and complete.

headings.title: Impounding, holding, and humane destruction of uncollared dogs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14554, A. 1949 S.B. 1097; prior revision 1929 § 12877). Directs incorporated city or town marshals to impound uncollared dogs running at large in a suitable posted location, hold them for one week, and put them to death by humane methods after that period. Independent review revised title to specify uncollared dogs running at large rather than over-generalizing to all dogs.

headings.title: Redemption of impounded dogs and fee disposition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits owners to redeem impounded dogs upon paying the required tax and a $5 redemption fee, allows the marshal to retain $2 per fee, and requires monthly remittance of the balance on the first day of each month to the county treasurer under sections 273.040 to 273.180.

headings.title: Penalty for marshal failure or refusal to impound
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes a city or town marshal's failure or refusal to take up and impound covered dogs a misdemeanor punishable upon conviction by a fine of $5 to $25.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14554, A. 1949 S.B. 1097; 1929 § 12877) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked city/town marshal impounding duty for uncollared dogs running at large, one-week holding period and humane destruction, $5 redemption fee ($2 marshal retention, monthly county remittance), and misdemeanor fine for marshal refusal. Revised subsection 1 to specify uncollared dogs; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Eligibility, deadline, and affidavit contents for damage claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (5) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14549, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Conditions recovery from the county dog license fund on an owner or custodian applying within ten days with two credible county residents (not kin by blood or marriage and not in the applicant's employ) by affidavit to the county clerk stating residency, ownership/custody, legal description of premises, livestock/poultry details, and market value.

headings.title: Filing for county commission review and owner-dog exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the county clerk to file received applications and affidavits for examination and judgment by the county commission, while excluding claims for destruction of livestock or poultry by a dog belonging to the livestock or poultry owner.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1) to (5) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14549, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked ten-day filing deadline, two-resident affidavit witness restrictions, thirty-day county residency, county commission review, and the exclusion for losses caused by the owner's own dog. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Petition and election order to adopt dog license tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14558, A. 1949 S.B. 1097, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971; prior revision 1929 § 12881). Requires a county commission, upon presentation of a petition signed by 100 or more county voters at a regular or special session, to order submission of the dog license tax adoption question at the next election; distinct from repeal in section 273.180.

headings.title: Ballot form for adopting dog license tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the ballot question block and history note. Prescribes the substantial ballot form for voting on whether to adopt a license tax on dogs.

headings.title: Majority adoption vote, publication, and operative date
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Upon a majority affirmative vote, requires the county commission to enter the result on its records and publish notice in a county newspaper, making the dog license tax law operative from publication.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including the ballot form block and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14558, A. 1949 S.B. 1097, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971; 1929 § 12881) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked 100-voter petition, ballot form, majority-vote adoption, newspaper publication, operative timing, and clear distinction from repeal under section 273.180. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Petition and election order to repeal dog license tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1941 p. 345 § 14558a, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Requires a county commission, upon presentation of a petition signed by 100 or more county voters at a regular or special session, to order submission of the question of repealing the dog license tax at the next election; distinct from adoption in section 273.170.

headings.title: Ballot form for repealing dog license tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the ballot question block and history note. Prescribes the substantial ballot form for voting on whether to repeal the license tax on dogs.

headings.title: Majority repeal vote, publication, and effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Upon a majority vote favoring repeal, requires the county commission to spread the result upon its records and publish notice in a county newspaper, rendering the dog license tax law inoperative in that county upon publication.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including the ballot form block and history note (L. 1941 p. 345 § 14558a, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Short title for sections 273.325 to 273.357
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 1). Designates sections 273.325 to 273.357 as the Animal Care Facilities Act.

headings.title: Definitions for sections 273.325 to 273.357
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including all nineteen subdivisions (1) to (19) and history note. Defines terms governing the Animal Care Facilities Act, including adequate food/housing/water, animal (dogs or cats), shelters, kennels, commercial and hobby/show breeders, dealers, humane euthanasia, intact female, pet shop, pound, state veterinarian, and USDA.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including all nineteen definitions (1) to (19) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 1) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked exact statutory range (sections 273.325 to 273.357) for both the Animal Care Facilities Act short title and definitions. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Grounds to refuse, not renew, or revoke licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (4) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 2 subsecs. 2, 3, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795). Grants the director permissive authority ("may") to refuse issuance or renewal or revoke a license on four enumerated grounds, including deliberate application misstatements, Act or rule violations, animal-treatment convictions, and failure to provide adequate food, water, housing, or sanitary facilities.

headings.title: Prohibition on nonprofit personnel for inspection or licensing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Bars the department of agriculture from retaining, contracting with, or otherwise utilizing personnel of any nonprofit organization to inspect or license listed animal facilities or breeders under sections 273.325 to 273.357.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for unlicensed operation or activity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes operating specified animal facilities (shelter, pound, kennels, pet shop, or exhibition facility) or acting as a commercial breeder or dealer without a valid license a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1) to (4) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 2 subsecs. 2, 3, A.L. 2010 S.B. 795) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive ("may") refusal/nonrenewal/revocation grounds, bar on using nonprofit personnel for inspections or licensing, and class A misdemeanor for unlicensed facility operation or breeder/dealer activity. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Exemption for breeders with three or fewer intact females
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 2 subsecs. 9, 10). Exempts persons engaged in breeding dogs and cats who harbor "three or less" intact females from sections 273.325 to 273.357.

headings.title: Hobby or show breeder exemption and free annual registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts hobby or show breeders from licensure and inspection under sections 273.325 to 273.357, requires the director to develop a registration form, and requires annual no-cost registration to establish hobby or show breeder status.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 2 subsecs. 9, 10) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked breeder exemption for harboring "three or less" intact females and hobby/show breeder licensure/inspection exemption paired with free annual director registration. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: USDA standards for federally licensed persons and facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 1, 2). Requires persons and facilities subject to USDA licensure to comply with USDA standards and regulations as revised from time to time.

headings.title: Director rules for non-USDA licensees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) to (3) and history note. Requires persons and facilities subject to sections 273.325 to 273.357 that are not subject to USDA licensure to comply with director-promulgated rules on adequate shelter (sanitation and ventilation), adequate food and water, and acquisition/disposition records.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1) to (3) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 1, 2) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked distinction between USDA-licensed persons/facilities following revised USDA standards and non-USDA licensees following director rules on shelter, food/water, and acquisition/disposition records. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Short title
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2010 Adopted by Initiative, Proposition B, Nov. 2, 2010; A.L. 2011 S.B. 113 & 95; A.L. 2011 S.B. 161; effective 4-27-11). Designates section 273.345 as the Canine Cruelty Prevention Act.

headings.title: Statutory purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States the act's purpose of prohibiting cruel and inhumane treatment of dogs bred in large-scale operations by requiring listed basic care standards.

headings.title: Care standards for breeding over ten female covered dogs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) to (6) and history note. Applies to any person with custody or ownership of more than ten female covered dogs for breeding and selling offspring as pets, requiring six specified standards of food/water, veterinary care, housing, space, regular exercise, and rest between breeding cycles.

headings.title: Definitions for section 273.345
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) to (10) and paragraphs (a) to (c) of subdivision (10) and history note. Defines ten section-specific terms notwithstanding section 273.325, including covered dog, retail pet store, necessary veterinary care, regular exercise, sufficient housing (with cleaning and compatibility rules), and sufficient space.

headings.title: Two-year veterinary and sales record retention and access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires persons subject to section 273.345 to maintain veterinary and sales records for the most recent previous two years and make them available upon request to the state veterinarian, a state or local animal welfare official, or a law enforcement agent.

headings.title: Cumulative effect, local authority, and scope exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Clarifies that section 273.345 adds to other state/federal animal welfare laws, preserves local animal welfare laws, places no numerical limit on dogs not used for breeding and selling offspring as pets, excludes listed temporary veterinary/research/transport/cleaning/exercise/emergency situations, and preserves hunting and sporting dog activities.

headings.title: Phased enclosure space, outdoor run, and flooring standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) to (c) and history note. Sets phased-in enclosure rules: historical 2012–2015 double-space standard for pre-April 15, 2011 enclosures, triple-space standard for post-April 15, 2011 enclosures and all enclosures as of January 1, 2016, attached outdoor run access except as prescribed by rule, department rule compliance, and wire-strand flooring prohibition.

headings.title: Severability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Declares the provisions and applications of section 273.345 severable if any part or application is held invalid or unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all eight subsections including all subdivisions/paragraphs and history/effective-date notes (Proposition B Nov. 2, 2010; A.L. 2011 S.B. 113 & 95; A.L. 2011 S.B. 161; effective 4-27-11) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked more-than-ten female covered dog threshold, section-specific definitions notwithstanding section 273.325, two-year record access, cumulative/local-law/hunting/temporary exclusions, subsection 7 phase-in dates (2012–2015 double space for pre-April 15, 2011 enclosures; triple space and wire-strand flooring prohibition for post-April 15, 2011 enclosures and all enclosures as of January 1, 2016; outdoor-run rule exception), and severability. Retained all eight titles as accurate and comprehensive.

headings.title: Health and veterinary care rules, pound exception, and records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 3, 4). Directs the director to promulgate health and veterinary care program rules for animals in the custody of licensees under sections 273.325 to 273.357, explicitly excepting pounds or dog pounds, and requires veterinary service records to be maintained and made available on request to the state veterinarian or an animal welfare official.

headings.title: Limit on construction requirements in rules covering pounds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits "any such rules promulgated to cover pounds or dog pounds" from requiring new building construction or major physical-plant reconstruction beyond normal upkeep and repair; retains exact archived text alongside subsection 1's pound exception.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 3, 4) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked subsection 1 health/veterinary care rulemaking and records with its explicit exception for pounds or dog pounds, alongside subsection 2 prohibiting "any such rules promulgated to cover pounds or dog pounds" from requiring new building construction or major physical-plant reconstruction beyond normal upkeep; archived textual tension preserved without alteration. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Circuit court injunctive, remedial, and civil penalty actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2011 S.B. 113 & 95, A.L. 2011 S.B. 161; effective 4-27-11). Authorizes the director, upon findings of uncorrected past violations of sections 273.325 to 273.357 (including operating without a valid section 273.327 license), to request the attorney general or county/circuit prosecutor to seek circuit court injunctive or remedial relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per separate violation.

headings.title: Elements and misdemeanor penalties for canine cruelty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Defines the crime of canine cruelty (repeated violations of sections 273.325 to 273.357 posing substantial risk to animal health and welfare, or knowingly violating an agreed-to remedial order) as a class C misdemeanor, elevated to a class A misdemeanor upon a prior guilty plea, nolo contendere plea, or finding of guilt.

headings.title: Criminal prosecution authority in circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the attorney general, county prosecuting attorney, or circuit attorney to bring criminal actions under sections 273.325 to 273.357 in circuit court in the county where the crime occurred.

headings.title: Preservation of actions under 578.012 and 273.329(3)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. States that no action under section 273.347 prevents or precludes action under section 578.012 or section 273.329(3).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 2011 S.B. 113 & 95, A.L. 2011 S.B. 161; effective 4-27-11) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Licensee premises open for inspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 5, 6, 7). Requires that the premises of each licensee be open for inspection.

headings.title: Disease quarantine, removal restrictions, and treatment procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) to (5) and continuation sentences and history note. Authorizes immediate quarantine and separation upon finding highly contagious, communicable, or infectious disease or exposure until resolved by one of five listed outcomes, bars removal of quarantined animals under treatment or testing until licensee notification and release, and places disease-elimination methods under state veterinarian discretion.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for violating sections 273.344 to 273.348
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Classifies any violation of sections 273.344 to 273.348 as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1) to (5) and continuation sentences in subdivision (5), plus history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 3 subsecs. 5, 6, 7), and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked open-premises inspection, disease quarantine triggers and release outcomes, removal prohibition until licensee notice and release, state veterinarian treatment discretion, and class A misdemeanor scope (sections 273.344 to 273.348). Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Advisory committee duties, unpaid service, and thirteen members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (13) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 4 subsecs. 2 to 6, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Establishes a thirteen-member director-appointed advisory committee to assist in establishing rules under sections 273.350 and 273.352 and provide ongoing review of sections 273.325 to 273.357, with no compensation or expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness conditioned on section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Conditions the effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under the authority of chapter 273 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1) to (13) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 4 subsecs. 2 to 6, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Exemption for veterinarian-supervised hospitals and boarding facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 5). Exempts establishments operating under the immediate supervision and control of a duly licensed veterinarian for animal hospitalization or boarding from sections 273.325 to 273.357.

headings.title: Licensing and rulemaking limits for research facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States that sections 273.325 to 273.357 do not require licensing of research facilities or authorize rules affecting the design, outlines, guidelines, or performance of actual research or experimentation as determined by the facility's institution animal care and use committee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 5) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Pre-release sterilization or written sterilization agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (2), paragraphs (a) to (e), subparagraphs a. to c., and history/footnote notes (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 8; Revisor footnote: *Word "after" appears in original rolls, referencing "contained in* the written policy" in subparagraph c.). Requires sterilization provisions for dogs and cats released by covered shelters or animal control agencies via either pre-custody veterinarian sterilization or a written sterilization agreement with five mandatory elements and completion-date formulas.

headings.title: Adopter sterilization deadline and permitted extensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/footnote notes. Requires adopters signing a sterilization agreement to complete sterilization by the stated date, permits extension to the next non-weekend/non-holiday day, and allows unlimited thirty-day extensions by the releasing agency upon a licensed veterinarian's letter or telephone report that sterilization may jeopardize the animal's life or health.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1) to (2), paragraphs (a) to (e), subparagraphs a. to c., history note (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 8), and original-rolls footnote (*Word "after" appears in original rolls for "contained in* the written policy" in (1)(2)(e)c.), and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked pre-release sterilization versus written sterilization agreement elements, completion-date rules, weekend/holiday extension, and unlimited thirty-day veterinary health extensions. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Transfer of title, possession, and control upon compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1992 S.B. 636 § 9). Requires each releasing agency to agree to give title, possession, and control of the animal so long as the adopter complies with the adoption agreement terms and conditions.

headings.title: Written veterinary confirmation of sterilization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/footnote notes. Directs the releasing agency to consider the animal sterilized upon receiving signed written confirmation from the licensed veterinarian who performed the sterilization.

headings.title: Owner-claimed animal clause and stricter local ordinance exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/footnote notes. Preserves the exact archived wording ("Exceptions to the sterilization requirements of sections 273.400 to 273.405 shall not apply to a dog or cat that is claimed from a releasing agency by a person who already owns the animal") without rewriting that drafting quirk, and covers the second sentence excluding releasing agencies in political subdivisions with ordinances exceeding sections 273.400 to 273.405. headings.title: Payment of sterilization costs by adopter or purchaser
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/footnote notes. Assigns all sterilization costs under sections 273.400 to 273.405 to the prospective adopter or purchaser unless otherwise provided.

headings.title: Exception and statement for hunting or livestock canines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/footnote notes (Revisor footnote: *Words "they are" appear in original rolls, referencing "he is* going to use"). Exempts department-rule breeds of canines used for lawful hunting or livestock production or management from sections 273.400 to 273.405 and allows adopters to sign a use statement in lieu of a sterilization agreement.

headings.title: Mandated reporters, one-day hotline reporting, and reasonable cause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/expiration notes (L. 2026 H.B. 2292; Expires 12-31-30). Requires listed professionals and foster-care advocacy personnel/volunteers with reasonable cause to suspect animal abuse or neglect to report to the Missouri Animal Control Association (MACA) or successor hotline within one day, and defines "reasonable cause" for this section.

headings.title: Information hotline workers must request for reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) to (4) and history/expiration notes. Lists four categories of animal, owner/caregiver, abuse/neglect, and supporting information hotline workers must request.

headings.title: Forwarding hotline reports to law enforcement and investigators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/expiration notes. Directs MACA or a successor entity to provide received reports to duly-authorized law enforcement officials and, if appropriate, county or municipal animal control officers or POST-certified or MACA-certified animal cruelty investigators.

headings.title: Good-faith civil and criminal immunity for mandated reporters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/expiration notes. Grants civil and criminal liability immunity in connection with required reports, expressly qualified by acting in good faith.

headings.title: Confidentiality of reporter-identifying information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/expiration notes. Declares information identifying a reporter confidential, not a public record, and exempt from section 109.180 and chapter 610 notwithstanding contrary law.

headings.title: Knowing false reports, section 575.080 penalties, and defenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/expiration notes.
